lines: Digital delay with four routing modes, a clock sync, an infinite loop and a choice of tape or fade time modulation
Sets how much of the delay output goes back into the delay input, reaching 125% at the clockwise end of the pink arc, with a short span at the join of the two arcs where it snaps to exactly 100%
Sweeps the delay time from 5ms to 2.73 seconds, or, once a clock is patched into SYNC, picks one of the multiplications and divisions of that clock marked around it
Mixes the dry signal against the delayed signal on an equal-power curve, dry alone at fully counter-clockwise and delay alone at fully clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the feedback CV input; at the centre that voltage has no effect, and turned counter-clockwise a positive voltage cuts the feedback
Attenuates and inverts the left delay time CV input; with that jack empty it holds 5V, so this knob then offsets the left delay time from the time knob
Attenuates and inverts the right delay time CV input, which sets the right delay time apart from the left one; in single delay mode it changes nothing
Attenuates and inverts the dry/wet CV input; turned counter-clockwise a positive voltage makes the mix drier, and turned clockwise it makes the mix wetter
Switches the infinite loop on, which shuts the audio inputs off and feeds each delay from its own output, or from the other delay's output in ping-pong mode; the button lights while the loop runs
Picks how a change of delay time is made: tape mode resamples the delay line and bends the pitch with it, and fade mode crossfades into the new time
Steps through the four delay modes, dual, ping-pong, single with send and return, and cascade with send and return, each shown by one of the lamps beside it
Modulates the feedback amount, scaled by the feedback attenuverter
Modulates the left delay time, scaled by the left time attenuverter; with nothing patched here the jack is held at 5V
A high gate switches the infinite loop on; with a clock at SYNC the loop starts on the next clock edge, and the button shows a dim light until then
Modulates the right delay time, scaled by the right time attenuverter; with nothing patched here it takes whatever is at the left delay time CV input
Modulates the dry and wet balance, scaled by the dry/wet attenuverter
The audio input to the left delay in dual and ping-pong modes, and the single audio input in single and cascade modes
The audio input to the right delay in dual and ping-pong modes, taking the left input when it is empty; in single and cascade modes it is the return of the feedback loop, normalled to the send
A clock here puts the module into sync mode, where the time knob picks a multiplication or division of that clock; sync mode holds until the cable is pulled out, even if the clock stops
The left delay in dual and ping-pong modes, carrying an even mix of both delays while the right output is empty; in single and cascade modes it is the delay output
The right delay in dual and ping-pong modes; in single and cascade modes it is the send, taken from inside the feedback loop
Menu — the loop button can act as a toggle, one press starting the loop and the next ending it, or as a momentary button that holds the loop only while it is pressed
Menu — the sync prescaler divides or multiplies the clock at SYNC before the time knob divides or multiplies it again
Chronoblob2.notes: The plugin is closed source, so nothing here was read from code. The mode and menu wording is from the installed binary: the delay modes are named Dual, Ping-pong, Single with send/return and Cascade with send/return, the time modulation switch is named Resampling and Crossfading where the hardware panel and manual say tape and fade, and the context menu carries Loop button behavior (Toggling or Momentary) and Sync prescaler. Where the hardware has a settings editor entered by holding the delay mode button, this plugin puts those two settings on the context menu instead, and the 2.0.0 changelog records that a delay mode selector was taken off that menu. The delay range of 5ms to 2.73 seconds, the 125% feedback maximum with its snap to 100%, the equal-power dry/wet curve and the normalling of the time CV inputs are all from the Chronoblob2 hardware manual version 1.3, and could not be checked against the plugin. The hardware manual's 0.7V threshold on the loop gate and its firmware update procedure are left out, being electrical and hardware-only. The panel carries almost no lettering: SYNC is the only word on it, and every other control is marked with an icon.

lines: Bitcrusher and decimator side by side, each built on a sample and hold, each with its own dry/wet mix and voltage control
Sets the depth of the bitcrushing
Sets the depth of the decimation by setting the rate of the internal oscillator that samples the signal
Crossfades between the unprocessed signal and the bitcrushed signal, in a straight line rather than an equal-power curve
Crossfades between the unprocessed signal and the decimated signal, in a straight line rather than an equal-power curve
Attenuates and inverts the bitcrusher's depth CV input
Attenuates and inverts the decimator's depth CV input, and fully counter-clockwise the decimator's sampling oscillator tracks that input at one volt per octave
Attenuates and inverts the CV input for the bitcrusher's dry and wet balance
Attenuates and inverts the CV input for the decimator's dry and wet balance
The audio input to the bitcrusher
The audio input to the decimator; with nothing patched here it takes the bitcrusher's output
Modulates the depth of the bitcrushing, scaled by the attenuverter for it
Modulates the depth of the decimation, scaled by the attenuverter for it
Modulates the dry and wet balance of the bitcrusher, scaled by the attenuverter for it
Modulates the dry and wet balance of the decimator, scaled by the attenuverter for it
A trigger steps the bitcrusher's sample and hold; it is combined with the bitcrusher's own internal trigger, so feeding the input signal in here forces a static waveform
A trigger samples the decimator, overriding its internal sampling oscillator for as long as a cable is patched here
The bitcrushed signal, mixed with the dry signal by the dry/wet control of the bitcrusher
The decimated signal, mixed with the dry signal by the dry/wet control of the decimator
T-Wrex.notes: The plugin is closed source. The normalling of the decimator input to the bitcrusher output, and the sample trigger overriding the internal one, are the maker's own tooltips in the installed build. The panel prints IN, SYNC, SAMPLE and OUT and nothing else: the two sections are marked with icons, and the words STOMP and CHOMP appear only in the manual and the tooltips. The one volt per octave tracking of the decimator's oscillator at the counter-clockwise end of its depth attenuverter is from the T-Wrex hardware manual version 1.0 and could not be checked against the plugin; the maker does carry that fact in a tooltip on Zzzorb's pitch attenuverter but not on this one.

lines: Four-pole multimode filter with a VCA ahead of it, carrying lowpass at two slopes, bandpass, highpass and notch at once
Sets the cutoff frequency of the filter
Sets the resonance of the filter
Sets the gain of the VCA
Attenuates the pitch CV input, and at 100% the cutoff tracks that input at one volt per octave
Attenuates and inverts the frequency CV input
Attenuates and inverts the resonance CV input
Attenuates and inverts the VCA gain CV input
Moves the filter cutoff, one volt per octave with its attenuverter at 100%
Modulates the cutoff frequency, scaled by the attenuverter for it
Modulates the resonance, scaled by the attenuverter for it
Modulates the VCA gain, scaled by the attenuverter for it; with nothing patched here it takes whatever is at the frequency CV input
The audio input to the VCA
The audio input to the filter, which also carries the VCA output while no cable is patched into that jack
The VCA output, which is mixed into the filter input until a cable is patched here
The filter output at four poles, 24dB per octave lowpass
The filter output at two poles, 12dB per octave lowpass
The bandpass output of the filter
The highpass output of the filter
The notch output of the filter
Note — a polyphonic signal at an input is mixed down to one channel before it is processed
Zzzorb.notes: Zzzorb has no manual anywhere, and the plugin is closed source, so the entry is built from the panel, the maker's tooltips in the installed build and the shipped CHANGELOG.md. The tooltips give three facts that are nowhere else: the pitch attenuverter is one volt per octave at 100%, the VCA gain CV input is normalled to the frequency CV input, and the VCA output is normally mixed into the filter input. The changelog's 1.0.4 entry is where the mixdown of polyphonic inputs to one channel comes from, and it also records that patching the VCA output, rather than the pitch input, is what breaks the VCA to filter normalling. The panel carries no lettering at all: every control is marked with an icon, so the names used here are the maker's tooltip names. The 24dB and 12dB per octave figures are the slopes of a four-pole and a two-pole lowpass and are not printed anywhere by the maker.
